[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
George Glascoe died by 3 July 1589, when Geo Glascoe was buried at Holy Trinity, Berwick upon Tweed, Northumberland. The burial is indexed in the National Burial Index, from a transcription supplied by the Northumberland & Durham Family History Society.<ref name="berwick1589">National Burial Index for England & Wales, Geo Glascoe, Holy Trinity, Berwick upon Tweed, 3 July 1589; Northumberland & Durham Family History Society, Findmypast BMD/NBI/07401624. [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=BMD%2FNBI%2F07401624&tab=this Findmypast transcript], accessed 21 October 2026. Original parish register not inspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Age and family ===
The burial transcript supplies no age, parent, spouse or occupation. It does not establish his birth date or birthplace, Scottish origin, or exact date or place of death. Berwick is the recorded burial locality.<ref name="berwick1589" />

[[Glasgow-3023|Alan Glasgw]] was dead before 26 February 1495. Fatherhood would require George to have lived to roughly 94 or older. This is unusual but cannot be categorically excluded without an age for George; no record connects the men, so Alan is not selected as his father.

=== Mureistoun comparison ===
The 1589 burial excludes George from the adult George Glasgow who witnessed a baptism in [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]]'s household at Mid Calder in 1605. Identity with the George at Mureistoun in 1586 remains possible separately; no age or property link identifies him.<ref name="berwick1589" /><ref>James Maidment, ed., ''Analecta Scotica'', vol.1 (1834), article CXVI, pp.395–396,399, Calder act19 April1586 ([https://archive.org/details/analectascotica00maidgoog printed edition]); National Records of Scotland, Mid Calder OPR694/10 p.7,17 February1605 ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers/church-births-baptisms parish register collection]). These sources name the earlier Mureistoun man and later witness, respectively; their preferred shared identity is separate from the Berwick burial.</ref> Neither a parent nor a Scottish residence is established for George Glascoe by this comparison.

=== Distinct Norwich record ===
The FamilySearch record cited below names [[Glasko-16|Margaret Glasko]] of Norwich, not George. It does not support his burial or identity.
